questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to learn to ride a horse as an adult
How horses help people's physical and mental health
The history of horses in British farming and war
Why horses are often scared of people and dogs
questions.why: They discuss horse therapy, where interacting with horses is used to heal physical and mental illness.

questions.q: How do Neil and Georgie feel about riding horses?
options: They both love it
They have never ridden a horse
Neil was a bit scared, but Georgie used to love riding
Georgie was scared, but Neil rides every week
questions.why: Neil says he was a bit scared; Georgie used to ride a lot and loves horses.

questions.q: Which activity can help children with muscle disorders like cerebral palsy?
options: Feeling the horse's movement
Brushing the horse's hair
Feeding the horse
Watching horses from a distance
questions.why: Neil says feeling the horse's movement can help children with muscle disorders like cerebral palsy.

questions.q: Why are horses particularly suitable for therapy, according to Georgie?
options: They are easy to train in a short time
They are very strong and can carry adults
They live for a long time with one family
They are very sensitive to human emotions
questions.why: She says horses are particularly suitable as they're very sensitive to human emotions.

questions.q: How did Claudia Nicholson's pony help her as a child?
options: It helped her win lots of riding competitions
It made her feel safe during a hard time
It helped her make new friends at school
It taught her to be less afraid of animals
questions.why: Going through puberty and her parents' separation, she felt 'met and safe and held' with the pony.

questions.q: Who does Claudia work with a lot at her centre?
options: Older people living alone
Professional riders
Teenage girls and children in care
Doctors and nurses
questions.why: Neil says she works a lot with teenage girls and children in care.

questions.q: What does Claudia say can happen when a traumatised child brushes a pony?
options: The child gets bored quickly and wants to leave
The pony becomes nervous and moves away
The child wants to ride the pony immediately
The child may cry, and the horse calms them
questions.why: She says they might want to have a cry they've been holding on to, and 'the horse regulates them'.

questions.q: What does Neil suggest makes horses 'perfect animal therapists'?
options: They notice our feelings and respond calmly
They can understand simple human words
They are much cheaper than human therapists
They really enjoy being brushed by people
questions.why: He says horses sense fear or sadness through breath, heart rate and movement, and respond calmly.
